# Strict fixed maximal-face witness count
witness construction in
`candidate 4a38a3cfd6733dce`.
Its finite midpoint-collapse mechanism is already present in the weighted
strict-face theorem and its colored extension in
`candidate 58dcf29bfb78a573`.
The contribution here is the exact saturation classification for the
fixed maximal occupied faces, and its all-circuit interface. This is not
an OC proof or a lattice-width classification.

## 1. Statement and hypotheses

Let I be a nonempty finite subset of Z^n, including n=0 if desired.
Assume only the following same-parity midpoint closure:

    p,q in I, p=q modulo 2  ==>  (p+q)/2 in I.        (1)

In particular (1) holds when I=conv(I) intersect Z^n. Set B=conv(I).
For p in B, let F(p) denote its minimal face in B, so
p belongs to relint F(p). Let F_1,...,F_s be all the distinct
inclusion-maximal members of {F(p): p in I}. Choose fixed witnesses
p_i in I with F(p_i)=F_i. Let k be the number of occupied parity
classes in I.

**Theorem.** The maximal occupied faces cover I and s<=k. Moreover,

    s=k  if and only if  I consists of exactly k vertices of B,
                         one in each occupied parity class.       (2)

Consequently, if I is not this exceptional vertex set, then

    s<=k-1.                                                       (3)

In particular |I|>k implies (3). In that situation k>=2.
All faces and relative interiors are taken in the actual affine hull;
no full-dimensionality assumption on B is needed.

## 2. Proof

First, for p,q in B and m=(p+q)/2, the minimal face F(m) is the
smallest face containing F(p) and F(q). Indeed any face containing m
contains both endpoints of its strict convex representation, hence
their minimal faces. Conversely any face containing both endpoints
contains m. We call this smallest face the join of F(p),F(q).

Every occupied minimal face is contained in a maximal member of the
finite family, so I is covered by the F_i. Suppose that points
r_i in I intersect relint F_i and r_j in I intersect relint F_j,
for distinct indices i,j, have the same parity. By (1) their midpoint
belongs to I, and its minimal face is the join of F_i,F_j. Distinct
maximal members are incomparable, so this occupied face strictly
contains both. This contradicts maximality. Thus the sets of parities
represented in the relative interiors of distinct F_i are disjoint.
In particular the chosen witnesses have distinct parities and s<=k.

We will also use the following matching-parity fact, which does not
require saturation: if q in I has the same parity as p_i, then q lies
in F_i. Its integer midpoint with p_i belongs to I, and the midpoint's
minimal face is the join of F(q),F_i. It contains F_i, so maximality
forces that join to equal F_i; hence q belongs to F_i.

Now assume s=k. The witness parities exhaust all occupied parities.
If r in I belongs to relint F_i, its parity must be that of p_i.
Otherwise its parity is that of some p_j with j!=i, and the preceding
matching-parity fact puts r in F_j. Then F_i=F(r) is contained in F_j,
contradicting the distinct maximality of these two faces.

Take any q in I with the parity of p_i. We already know q belongs to
F_i. Define q_h=p_i+2^(-h)(q-p_i) for h=1,2,... . The point q_1 is an
integer midpoint and belongs to I by (1). It is in relint F_i because
p_i is in that relative interior and q is in F_i. By the previous
paragraph q_1 has the parity of p_i. Induction now shows that every
q_h is an integer point of I intersect relint F_i of that same parity:
q_(h+1) is the midpoint of p_i and q_h. If q!=p_i, these are infinitely
many distinct points, contradicting the finiteness of I. Therefore
each occupied parity class consists of its single witness, and
I={p_1,...,p_k}.

Finally each F_i is a singleton vertex. Choose a vertex v of F_i.
It is a vertex of B, and every vertex of the convex hull of a finite
set belongs to that set. Thus v=p_j for some j. Its minimal face is
F_j={v}, which is maximal among occupied faces and is contained in
F_i. Hence F_i=F_j={v}. This proves the forward direction of (2).
Conversely, if I consists of k vertices with different parities, all
occupied minimal faces are precisely those k singleton vertices, so
s=k. The strict conclusion follows because s,k are integers.

This also covers k=1: s>=1 and s<=k force saturation and a singleton.
The case n=0 therefore introduces no additional convention.

## 3. Sharpness of the strict count

For each integer k>=2 work in Z^(k-1) and put

    B=conv{0,2e_1,e_2,...,e_(k-1)}.

Its complete integer set is

    I={0,e_1,2e_1,e_2,...,e_(k-1)}.                    (4)

Indeed B is specified by x_i>=0 and
x_1/2+sum_(i>=2)x_i<=1. An integer point either has one coordinate
i>=2 equal to one and all other coordinates zero, or has all those
coordinates zero and x_1 equal to 0,1,2. This proves (4).
There are k occupied parities and k+1 points. The maximal occupied
faces are the edge [0,2e_1], occupied in its relative interior by e_1,
and the k-2 singleton vertices e_2,...,e_(k-1). Hence s=k-1.
The strict count cannot be improved in terms of k alone.

The faces in a general nonsaturated configuration may overlap on
proper faces. The theorem does not turn their cover into a partition.
Nor does saturation force width one or a cube: the audited
16-vertex width-two example in
`candidate 067c3a013000fe6d`
already rules out that additional conclusion.

## 4. Exact critical-cover consequence and its scope

Use precisely the full mixed d-volume hypotheses, d>=1, of
`candidate 4a38a3cfd6733dce`,
Sections 2--5. In particular M>0, I is the finite set of integer bases
supporting an actual deepest point, and the cited source proves that I
is complete in its convex hull. Its positive continuous-dimensional
fibers, actual critical caps, and critical contact argument imply that
every critical circuit at p_i covers the entire continuous plane over
F_i. Thus any selection of one circuit at each of these FIXED witnesses
covers all deepest fibers.

If I is not exactly a vertex set with one point per occupied parity,
the number of witnesses in this universal statement is at most k-1.
For the exact quantile deformations covered by that source's Section 4,
including its explicit section-convergence and slack-group conditions,
the comparison is therefore

    D(S_t) <= max_(1<=i<=s) tau_i(t)/M_t,
    s<=k-1.                                             (5)

This is still a cover of every actual new fiber: the original
nondeep groups and the emerging zero-volume-base groups are retained
as in that source. Reducing the deepest witness count does not permit
their omission.

Under the additional signed linear variation hypotheses of its
Sections 5--6, at a local minimum its universal circuit response sets
Gamma_i have a nonempty essential subset J satisfying

    dim span(union_(i in J)Gamma_i)
      <=|J|-1<=s-1<=k-2.                                (6)

This follows directly by inserting the strict count into the proved
independent-representative argument there. In particular, if k=2 and
the exceptional vertex configuration is absent, there is one fixed
witness and all its relevant signed-linear responses vanish.

Neither (5) nor (6) is a cap-mass estimate or a descent theorem. No
unrestricted minimizer is asserted to exist. The arithmetic theorem
itself is dimension-free, but this critical-cover application retains
the cited full mixed d-volume hypotheses; it does not silently extend
the critical-contact construction to nonparallel intrinsic fibers.
